pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c8146b302e7948bf6db8e as of 2026-09-02T05:44:45.702Z: {"title":"23️⃣ SQL Interview Master Bank — CASE, Subqueries & CTEs"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🎯"} دور الصفحة اتغيّر: كانت شبه نسخة مكررة من \🎯](https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c81d5835be46fca54ec8a%22%3E%F0%9F%8E%AF) 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns\ (نفس الأسئلة، نفس الـframework، نفس الـEXISTS pattern، نفس الـred flags — بس بلغة إنجليزية). دلوقتي هي field manual مختصر يتماشى مع دور مكتبة SQL — Practical Reference Toolkit: quick lookup سريع بدون شرح مطوّل. للمراجعة العميقة (Q&A كامل + framework + traps + كود جاهز)، روح لصفحة 99. ## Quick Drill — Define in one sentence CASE, EXISTS, IN, scalar subquery, derived table, correlated subquery, nested subquery, CTE, window function, conditional aggregation. ## One-liners worth remembering - Simple vs Searched CASE: simple compares one expression to multiple values; searched evaluates independent Boolean conditions. - Correlated subquery: references a column from the outer query scope. Nested describes structure, not dependency — not every nested subquery is correlated. - CTE ≠ automatic performance win. Performance depends on the engine, optimizer, and execution plan. - AVG(CASE ... ELSE 0 END) turns excluded rows into valid zeros — usually you want ELSE NULL. - Prefer a window function over a subquery when you need the row-level detail and an analytic value (rank, running total, group comparison) together. ## Coding Challenge Titles (full walkthroughs in page 99) 1. Conditional KPI — completion rate per month (COUNT, SUM(CASE...), careful denominator). 2. Above-average customers (scalar subquery vs CTE vs window function — global or segment-specific average?). 3. Customers with recent activity (EXISTS — question is about existence, not retrieving rows). 4. Average of monthly totals — trap: AVG(sale_amount) ≠ AVG(monthly_total). ## Interview Answer Framework (same as page 99) Business meaning → population → grain → joins → transformation → aggregation/window → edge cases → validation → performance. Full Q&A, red flags, senior-level reasoning prompts, and ready-to-use SQL patterns: see \🎯](https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c81d5835be46fca54ec8a%22%3E%F0%9F%8E%AF) 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns\.

pages.title: 🎯 🎯 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c81d5835be46fca54ec8a as of 2026-09-02T05:44:29.592Z: {"title":"🎯 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🎯"} # Purpose مرجع مقابلات عملي يغطي CASE, Subqueries, Correlated/Nested Subqueries, CTEs، والاختيارات البديلة بينها. # 1. Core Interview Questions ### Q0. ما الفرق بين Simple CASE وSearched CASE؟ Simple CASE: بتقارن تعبير واحد بقيم متعددة. Searched CASE: بتقيّم شروط Boolean مستقلة في كل WHEN ... THEN. ### Q1. What is the difference between a simple, correlated, and nested subquery? - Simple / uncorrelated: لا تعتمد على outer query. - Correlated: تستخدم قيمة من outer query. - Nested: Subquery داخل Subquery أخرى؛ هذا يصف structure وليس dependency. ### Q2. Is every nested subquery correlated? No. Nesting and correlation are different dimensions. A query can be nested but fully uncorrelated. ### Q3. When would you choose EXISTS instead of IN? عندما يكون السؤال منطقياً: "هل يوجد على الأقل صف مرتبط؟"؛ EXISTS يعبر عن intent بوضوح ولا يحتاج إلى إرجاع قائمة قيم إلى المستوى الخارجي. ### Q4. CTE vs subquery — what is the difference? CTE غالبًا أوضح للقراءة والتنظيم، خصوصًا عند وجود مراحل متعددة. لكن CTE ليست تلقائيًا أسرع؛ الأداء يعتمد على الـoptimizer والـdialect وخطة التنفيذ. ### Q5. When is a window function better than a subquery? عندما تريد قيمة محسوبة على مجموعة من الصفوف مع الاحتفاظ بنفس الصفوف التفصيلية، مثل الفرق عن المتوسط أو ranking. ### Q6. Why can AVG(CASE ... ELSE 0 END) be wrong? لأن الصفوف التي لا تنتمي إلى population المطلوبة تدخل في denominator كأصفار. غالبًا نحتاج NULL للحالات المستبعدة. # 2. Interview Traps - الخلط بين COUNT(*) وCOUNT(column). - اعتبار ELSE مجرد fallback نصي بدون التفكير في الـpopulation. - نسيان alias للـderived table. - استخدام WHERE بعد aggregation بطريقة تغير معنى السؤال. - المقارنة بين AVG(row-level metric) وAVG(group-level metric) وكأنهما نفس الشيء. - افتراض أن CTE أو subquery أو JOIN أسرع دائمًا. - تجاهل تأثير duplicate rows بعد JOIN. - نسيان أن NULL يغيّر سلوك COUNT, AVG, comparisons، وبعض predicates. # 3. Real-World Pattern: Win Rate ```sql AVG( CASE WHEN outcome = 'Win' THEN 1 WHEN outcome = 'Loss' THEN 0 ELSE NULL END ) ``` الفكرة العامة: percentage = average of a 0/1 indicator عندما تكون population والـNULL semantics صحيحة. # 4. Real-World Pattern: Customers Above Segment Average ```sql WITH customer_spend AS ( SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS spend FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ), segment_avg AS ( SELECT segment, AVG(spend) AS avg_spend FROM customer_spend GROUP BY segment ) SELECT c.customer_id, c.spend FROM customer_spend c JOIN segment_avg s ON c.segment = s.segment WHERE c.spend > s.avg_spend; ``` # 5. Real-World Pattern: Existence Test ```sql SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days' ); ``` # 6. How to Explain a Complex Query in an Interview استخدم هذا الترتيب: 1. Business question 2. Population + grain 3. Input tables and joins 4. Intermediate transformations 5. Aggregation/window logic 6. NULL and edge-case behavior 7. Validation strategy 8. Performance considerations # 8. سيناريوهات تطبيقية إضافية ### مؤشر أداء شرطي (Conditional KPI) رجّع إجمالي الطلبات، الطلبات المكتملة، الملغاة، ومعدل الإكمال لكل شهر، باستخدام COUNT، SUM(CASE...)، ومؤشر 0/1 مع تحديد دقيق للـdenominator. ### فخ — متوسط الإجماليات الشهرية احسب المبيعات الشهرية، وقارن كل شهر بمتوسط الإجماليات الشهرية. AVG(sale_amount) مش زي AVG(monthly_total) — الأول متوسط على مستوى الصف، والتاني متوسط على مستوى المجموعة. ### Quick Drill — عرّف كل واحدة من دول بجملة واحدة CASE، EXISTS، IN، scalar subquery، derived table، correlated subquery، nested subquery، CTE، window function، conditional aggregation. # 9. Senior-Level Follow-Ups - How would you verify that a JOIN did not duplicate entities? - What indexes might support the filtering/join path? - What does the execution plan tell you? - Can the query be rewritten with a window function? - Can the logic be simplified with a CTE without changing semantics? - What happens when the comparison value is NULL? - How would you test correctness on boundary cases?

pages.title: ⚙️ 24️⃣ Advanced SQL Patterns — Correctness, Performance & Maintainability
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c8196a02ad41449f06ba8 as of 2026-09-23T15:44:57.489Z: {"title":"24️⃣ Advanced SQL Patterns — Correctness, Performance & Maintainability"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"⚙️"} Ownership. هذه الصفحة قائمة traps وأنماط مراجعة، مش مرجع كانوني ثالث. - Correctness → - Performance → - الأسئلة والـ traps تفضل هنا تحت . ## 1. Correctness Before Optimization Use this order: ```txt Semantics → Grain → Population → NULLs → Result shape → Performance ``` A fast query returning the wrong population is still wrong. ## 2. Anti-Duplication Pattern Before aggregating after a JOIN, ask whether the relationship is one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many. ```sql -- Validate expected uniqueness SELECT key, COUNT(*) FROM detail GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; ``` ## 3. EXISTS for Existence ```sql WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id ) ``` The subquery does not need to return business columns; existence is the intent. For a full worked example (customers active in the last 90 days), see the Existence Test pattern in \🎯](https://app.notion.com/p/3cd3906c5d6c81d5835be46fca54ec8a%22%3E%F0%9F%8E%AF) 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns\. ## 4. NOT EXISTS for Anti-Joins Useful for questions such as: > Find customers who have never placed an order. ```sql WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id ) ``` ## 5. CTE Layering Pattern Name each business step: ```txt raw_filtered ↓ entity_level ↓ group_level ↓ kpi_ready ``` This makes grain changes explicit and debugging easier. ## 6. When to Replace Deep Nesting Consider a CTE when: - nesting becomes difficult to read; - an intermediate result has a business meaning; - you need to debug a stage separately; - the same logical step is referenced multiple times where the dialect supports an appropriate strategy. ## 7. When to Consider a Window Function Use a window when you need both: - the row-level result, and - a comparison/aggregate over a related set of rows. Examples: rank within department, percent of total, running total, difference from average. ## 8. NULL-Safe Thinking Always ask: - Can this column be NULL? - Does NULL belong in the numerator? - Does NULL belong in the denominator? - Does the predicate still express the intended business rule? ## 9. Performance Investigation Do not optimize by intuition alone. Compare alternatives using the database's execution plan and runtime metrics. Look for: - unexpected full scans; - poor join strategies; - high row counts early in the plan; - repeated expensive work; - missing/selectivity-poor indexes where appropriate; - unnecessary columns and joins. ## 10. Maintainability Rules Prefer SQL that makes business intent obvious: - meaningful aliases; - one clear responsibility per CTE; - consistent naming; - explicit columns rather than SELECT * in production logic; - comments for business rules, not obvious syntax. ## 11. Refactoring Test When rewriting a query from subquery → CTE or subquery → window function, compare: 1. row count, 2. distinct business keys, 3. min/max values, 4. NULL counts, 5. KPI totals, 6. edge cases. ## 12. Golden Rule > Choose the technique that makes the business logic easiest to verify; then use the execution plan to judge performance.

pages.title: 19 — SQL Interview Master Hub
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c8188bae4cc26576c250e as of 2026-09-23T21:28:45.251Z: {"title":"19 — SQL Interview Master Hub"} null ## خريطة الإجابة الأداء مجاش بعد ما النتيجة تبقى صحيحة. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["1 Output grain"] --> B["2 Tables and keys"] --> C["3 Population and filters"] --> D["4 Combine, collapse, or compare?"] D --> E["5 JOIN, GROUP BY, subquery, CTE, or window"] E --> F["6 NULL behavior"] --> G["7 Row counts and edge cases"] --> H["8 Performance"] ``` ## Purpose Central interview library for SQL. This page organizes interview preparation around concepts, reasoning, traps, and business problems rather than isolated syntax questions. ## 1. Interview Strategy Strong SQL interview performance is not just writing syntax. The interviewer is often testing whether you can: - define the grain - reason about relationships/cardinality - control the population - aggregate correctly - handle NULLs - choose the simplest appropriate technique - validate the result - explain trade-offs ## 2. Core Areas ### Foundations - logical query processing - SELECT / FROM / WHERE - DISTINCT - NULL and three-valued logic - data types and casting ### Relationships - INNER / LEFT / FULL / CROSS / SELF JOIN - one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many - row multiplication - ON vs WHERE - JOIN vs EXISTS ### Aggregation - GROUP BY - WHERE vs HAVING - COUNT vs COUNT(column) - conditional aggregation - pre-aggregation - ROLLUP / CUBE / GROUPING SETS ### Subqueries & CTEs - scalar subqueries - IN / EXISTS - correlated subqueries - derived tables - CTEs - nested queries ### Window Functions - PARTITION BY - ORDER BY - ranking - LAG / LEAD - running totals - frames ### Data Quality - duplicates - NULLs - orphan keys - domain/range validation - reconciliation ### Performance - sargability - indexes - execution plans - early filtering - join strategy ### DWH / BI - fact/dimension reasoning - grain - snapshots - incremental loads - KPI correctness ## 3. High-Value Comparison Questions | Question | What the interviewer is testing | | --- | --- | | JOIN vs EXISTS? | Relationship vs existence reasoning | | WHERE vs HAVING? | Filtering stage and grain | | UNION vs UNION ALL? | Set semantics and duplicates | | GROUP BY vs window function? | Collapse grain vs preserve grain | | CTE vs subquery? | Readability/decomposition vs syntax choice | | IN vs EXISTS? | Membership vs existence + NULL awareness | | NOT IN vs NOT EXISTS? | Three-valued logic and correctness | | DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP? | DML/DDL and operational impact | | WHERE predicate on LEFT JOIN? | Outer-join semantics | | DISTINCT as a fix? | Whether the candidate understands root cause | ## 4. Classic Business Problems Practice explaining and solving: 1. Top N customers per month. 2. Customers with no orders. 3. Second-highest salary. 4. Latest transaction per customer. 5. Running total by month. 6. Month-over-month growth. 7. Duplicate customer records. 8. Products never sold. 9. Students above average earned hours. 10. Enrollment reconciliation between source and warehouse. ## 5. Interview Answer Framework When asked to solve a SQL problem: 1. Clarify the desired output grain. 2. Identify the source tables and keys. 3. State the population/filter logic. 4. Decide whether rows should be combined, collapsed, or compared. 5. Choose JOIN / aggregation / subquery / CTE / window function accordingly. 6. Check NULL behavior. 7. Validate row counts and edge cases. 8. Explain performance considerations only after correctness is established. ## 6. Red Flags Interviewers Notice - blindly using DISTINCT - joining before understanding cardinality - using WHERE when HAVING is required - ignoring NULL semantics - using a correlated subquery without considering scale - claiming CTEs are always faster - optimizing before defining the correct result - giving a query without explaining the business logic ## 7. Practical Interview Drill For every question, write two answers: - Minimal correct solution - Production-aware solution with validation, edge cases, and performance considerations Then explain why you selected the technique. ## 8. What lives here This hub owns the question banks below. It is not a second canon. - Correctness theory → - Performance theory → 24 is the trap checklist. Modules 12 and 16 stay the canonical explanation.

pages.title: 🗄️ Temporary Tables — Complete Reference
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c81a3adaeddff44170644 as of 2026-09-01T12:46:23.636Z: {"title":"Temporary Tables — Complete Reference"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🗄️"} > جزء من سلسلة Intermediate SQL: هذا المرجع مخصص لـTemporary Tables — الإنشاء، الاستخدام، ومقارنتها بـCTE/Subquery/View. # 1. ليه نستخدم Temporary Tables؟ مفيدة عندما تريد: 1. الاحتفاظ بنتيجة intermediate query. 2. استخدام نفس intermediate dataset في أكثر من query. 3. تقسيم workflow معقد إلى مراحل واضحة. # 2. الإنشاء (Create) ```sql CREATE TEMP TABLE top_companies AS SELECT rank, title FROM fortune500 ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10; ``` ثم: ```sql SELECT * FROM top_companies; ``` الـ result يصبح temporary table مستقلة عن source table؛ ليست live link إلى نتيجة الـ source. # 3. إضافة صفوف (Insert Additional Rows) ```sql INSERT INTO top_companies (rank, title) SELECT rank, title FROM fortune500 WHERE rank BETWEEN 11 AND 20; ``` الـ SELECT يجب أن ينتج columns متوافقة مع target table. # 4. الحذف (Drop) ```sql DROP TABLE top_companies; ``` أو بشكل safer في scripts: ```sql DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_companies; ``` # 5. دورة الحياة (Lifecycle) ```txt CREATE TEMP TABLE ↓ Available in current session ↓ Use in multiple queries ↓ Disconnect ↓ Automatically removed ``` # 6. Temp Table مقابل CTE مقابل Subquery مقابل View | Technique | Scope | Main purpose | Can reuse in later statements? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Subquery | Part of a statement | Intermediate result inside query | No | | CTE | One statement | Readable multi-step query | No | | Temp Table | Session | Reusable intermediate dataset | Yes | | View | Persistent database object | Reusable saved query abstraction | Yes | ```txt Subquery → inside a query CTE → named step inside a statement Temp → temporary table across statements View → persistent saved query definition ``` # 7. حالة واقعية — بناء Intermediate Dataset قابل لإعادة الاستخدام السؤال: "اعمل analysis على أعلى العملاء إنفاقًا، ثم استخدم نفس القائمة في عدة analyses." ```sql -- Step 1 CREATE TEMP TABLE high_value_customers AS SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spend FROM sales GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) >= 100000; -- Step 2: عددهم SELECT COUNT(*) FROM high_value_customers; -- Step 3: متوسط الإنفاق SELECT AVG(total_spend) FROM high_value_customers; -- Step 4: استخدامهم مع customer attributes SELECT c.country, COUNT(*) AS high_value_customers FROM high_value_customers h JOIN customers c ON h.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY high_value_customers DESC; ``` هنا الـ Temp Table أصبحت reusable analytical population خلال الـ session. # 8. دليل القرار — أي أداة أستخدم؟ ### استخدم Subquery عندما: - تحتاج intermediate result داخل query واحدة. - المنطق صغير وواضح. ### استخدم CTE عندما: - Query فيها عدة logical steps وتحتاج readability وdebugging أسهل. ### استخدم Temp Table عندما: - تحتاج نفس intermediate dataset في عدة statements. - تريد تقسيم workflow طويل إلى مراحل، أو تريد inspect intermediate result أثناء التحليل. ### استخدم View عندما: - تحتاج abstraction/query reusable بشكل persistent لعدة مستخدمين. > Do not choose a technique فقط لأنها تعمل. Choose the technique that best matches scope, reuse, maintainability, and business need. # 9. أخطاء المقابلات والامتحانات - Temp Table vs CTE: الـCTE محصورة بـstatement واحد؛ الـTemp Table ممكن تُعاد استخدامها عبر statements متعددة في نفس الـsession. - Temp Table vs View: الـTemp Table بتخزن نتيجة وسيطة للـsession؛ الـView بتخزن تعريف query قابل لإعادة الاستخدام بشكل دائم. # 10. Cheat Sheet ```sql -- Temp table CREATE TEMP TABLE temp_name AS SELECT ...; -- Insert into temp table INSERT INTO temp_name SELECT ...; -- Safe drop DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp_name; ``` --- ### 🔗 مراجع ذات صلة

pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3ca3906c5d6c8196ade1dd080d67e6ee as of 2026-09-23T15:45:08.862Z: {"title":"Intermediate SQL — Comprehensive Guide"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧠"} Not canonical. Do not study from this page. المسار الحي هو ، والباب الوحيد هو SQL Master Library. # 📚 الصفحة الرئيسية — Intermediate SQL > 🗂️ خريطة المكتبة (Library Map) مصدر نظام الترقيم ده، وفيه خطة إعادة الهيكلة الكاملة. ### 🧭 00 — ابدأ من هنا (Start Here) ✅ يشرح workflow حل المشكلة، Grain/Population checks، اختيار التقنية، وResult-shape validation. ابدأ من هنا دايمًا. ### 🧱 01 — SQL Foundations ✅ المرجع الكانوني: mental model، grain، logical query processing order، WHERE vs HAVING، NULL/3VL، DISTINCT، keys، filtering principles، anti-patterns. 🔀 كانت نسخة مكررة بالخطأ — محتواها الفريد اتنقل للصفحة الكانونية فوق، ودلوقتي مجرد pointer ليها. ### 🗄️ 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling ✅ نقطة البداية مع أي database جديدة: schema، الجداول، العلاقات (PK/FK)، constraints. ✅ يغطي كمان أنواع البيانات الرقمية والـEDA الإحصائي (مركز، تشتت، percentiles، correlation) — جزء منه ينتمي لـ 13 Data Quality كمان. ### 🔠 03 — Data Types, Casting & NULL Logic ✅ type semantics، casting، NULL/3VL، NULL في aggregates وjoins. ### 🔎 04 — Filtering & Conditional Logic ✅ WHERE/predicate reasoning، CASE، filter placement. ✅ مرجع شامل قديم لسه موجود — قسم CASE منه بيتقاطع مع 04، وقسم Subqueries/CTEs بيتقاطع مع 07 تحت. ### 🔗 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning ✅ المرجع الكانوني: cardinality، fan-out/row multiplication، JOIN vs EXISTS/IN، LEFT JOIN filtering trap، bridge tables، self joins، DWH/BI correctness. 🔀 كانت نسخة مكررة بالخطأ — محتواها الفريد اتنقل فوق، ودلوقتي مجرد pointer. ### 📊 06 — Aggregation & Grouping ✅ المرجع الكانوني: GROUP BY كـgrain transformation، conditional aggregation، DISTINCT aggregation، semi-additive measures، ROLLUP/CUBE، KPI design. 🔀 كانت نسخة مكررة بالخطأ — محتواها الفريد اتنقل فوق، ودلوقتي مجرد pointer. ### 🧩 07 — Subqueries & CTEs ✅ المرجع الكانوني الشامل. المراجع المتخصصة التالية بتغطي تفاصيل فرعية: ### ➕ 08 — Set Operations ✅ UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT، set vs JOIN decisions. ### 📈 09 — Window Functions ✅ ranking، LAG/LEAD، frames، running/moving totals، paging، pivoting، ROLLUP/CUBE. ### 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics ✅ المرجع العام لبيانات التاريخ والوقت (نسخة PostgreSQL موجودة كـextension في مكتبة PostgreSQL المنفصلة). ### 🔤 11 — Text, String & Pattern Matching ✅ المرجع العام لبيانات النصوص (نفس الملاحظة: نسخة PostgreSQL منفصلة في مكتبتها الخاصة). ### 🧮 12 — Analytical SQL Patterns ✅ اتشذّبت من التكرار النظري وبقت applied/case-study layer صافي: قاعدة بيانات MovieNow، حالات بيزنس حقيقية، وحالة ختامية متكاملة بتستخدم ROLLUP في قرار استثماري فعلي. ### 🧪 13 — Data Quality & Validation ✅ يتقاطع جزئيًا مع الـEDA في موديول 02 — ده تكرار "صحي" (Learning Path ثم Reference) طالما مفيش نسخ كاملة متكررة. ### ⚙️ 14 — SQL Performance Engineering ✅ sargability، execution plans، indexing fundamentals، optimization anti-patterns. ### 🛠️ 15 — DDL / DML / Transactions ✅ database changes، write operations، ACID، isolation، safe-change patterns. ### 🏗️ 16 — Database Design ✅ normalization/denormalization، natural/surrogate/composite keys، referential actions. ### 🏬 17 — SQL for DWH / BI ✅ fact/dimension، grain، SCD، staging/ODS/core/semantic patterns، incremental loads. ### 🐘 18 — PostgreSQL Specialization 🌐 موجودة في مكتبة منفصلة (PostgreSQL Data Manipulation — Master Reference) — مقصود إنها extension مش نسخة تانية من نفس المفاهيم العامة. مفيش link مباشر من هنا لسه. ### 🎯 19 — Interview Master Hub ✅ المركز الرئيسي لأسئلة المقابلات. المراجع دي بتتغذى منها: ### 🧰 20 — Practical SQL Toolkit 🌐 موجودة في مكتبة منفصلة (SQL — Practical Reference Toolkit) كـfield manual سريع للشغل والمقابلات. مفيش link مباشر من هنا لسه. --- ## 🧠 النموذج الذهني الأساسي (Master Mental Model) ```txt Business Question ↓ Explore schema (PK/FK, constraints) + data types ↓ Population + Required Grain ↓ Tables / Relationships ↓ JOIN / Filter ↓ CASE / Subquery / CTE ↓ GROUP BY or Window Function ↓ NULL + Edge Cases ↓ Validate Result ↓ Execution Plan when performance matters ``` ## ⭐ القواعد الذهبية (Golden Rules) 1. افهم الـschema قبل أي حاجة تانية (Schema before everything). مين الجداول، إيه العلاقات، فين الـPK/FK. 2. حدد الـGrain قبل الصياغة (Grain before syntax). اكتب الجملة: One output row represents \_\_\_. 3. حدد الـPopulation قبل المقاييس (Population before metrics). اعرف مين يدخل الحساب ومين لا. 4. الـNULL جزء من المنطق (NULL is logic). لا تستخدم ELSE 0 تلقائيًا. 5. نوع الـCOUNT مهم (COUNT matters): COUNT(*) ليست نفسها COUNT(expression). 6. مستوى التجميع مهم (Aggregation level matters): متوسط الصفوف (average of rows) لا يساوي متوسط المجموعات (average of groups). 7. الـJOIN ممكن يضاعف الصفوف (JOIN can multiply rows). تحقق من الـcardinality قبل الـaggregation. 8. الفرق بين Nested وCorrelated: الـNested بيخص البنية (structure)، والـCorrelated بيخص الاعتمادية (dependency). 9. الـCTE بيحسّن التنظيم مش بالضرورة الأداء (performance). 10. الـWindow Functions بتحافظ على الصفوف (preserve rows). استخدمها لما تحتاج قيمة تحليلية (analytical value) جنب التفاصيل. 11. الـExecution Plan هو الحكم الحقيقي للأداء. ما تفترضش إن أقصر Query هي الأسرع. ## 🎓 مسارات الدراسة (Study Paths) مسار المراجعة السريعة (Fast Review): 00 → Core concept page → Quick Reference → Interview Master Bank. مسار التعلّم العميق (Deep Learning): 00 → 01 Foundations → 02 Schema/PK-FK → 03 Data Types → 04 Filtering/CASE → 05 JOINs → 06 Aggregation → 07 Subqueries/CTEs → 08 Set Operations → 09 Window Functions → 10 Date/Time → 11 Text. مسار المقابلات (Interview): Concept → Coding Challenge → Grain/Population explanation → Edge cases → Performance discussion. مسار العمل الفعلي (Real Work): Business question → Schema exploration → metric definition → SQL implementation → validation → production hardening. --- > مبدأ المكتبة (Library principle): افهم الـbusiness meaning أولًا، ثم اختر الـSQL construct الذي يجعل المنطق صحيحًا وقابلًا للفحص والصيانة.

pages.title: 🗺️ 🗺️ SQL Content Inventory — Coverage, Overlap & Gaps
pages.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c81c9a1a8eee6a887560e as of 2026-09-01T20:05:58.572Z: {"title":"🗺️ SQL Content Inventory — Coverage, Overlap & Gaps"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🗺️"} Purpose: جرد شامل لمحتوى SQL الموجود حاليًا في Notion قبل إعادة الهيكلة. الهدف هو معرفة: ماذا نغطي؟ أين يوجد؟ ما الذي يتكرر؟ وما الذي ينقصنا؟ ## 1. Executive Summary المشكلة الحالية ليست نقص المحتوى؛ بالعكس، عندك مكتبة SQL قوية وموزعة على أكثر من طبقة. التحدي الأساسي هو التداخل بين Learning Path وReference Library وPostgreSQL-specific notes وInterview notes. ### الطبقات الحالية 1. Learning Path: Intermediate SQL — Comprehensive Guide — المسار التعليمي الأساسي. 2. Practical Reference: SQL — Practical Reference Toolkit — lookup سريع للشغل والمقابلات. 3. PostgreSQL Specialization: PostgreSQL Data Manipulation — Master Reference — وظائف وميزات PostgreSQL الخاصة. 4. Analytics / Decision Making: SQL Data-Driven Decision Making — Comprehensive Analytics Reference — تطبيق SQL على أسئلة تحليلية وbusiness decisions. 5. Interview Layer: Interview Master Bank + Interview Questions/Traps + Advanced Patterns. ## 2. Current Content Inventory
Area Current Notes Coverage Main Issue
Learning Map / Mental Models Intermediate SQL + Learning Map 🟢 Strong مكرر جزئيًا مع decision frameworks
Database Exploration / Schema Database Exploration & Schema + Numeric/Constraints 🟢 Strong تقاطع مع PostgreSQL schema inspection
Data Types / Casting Numeric Data Types & Casting + PostgreSQL Data Types 🟢 Strong نفس المفاهيم موزعة حسب المستوى
Text / String Character/Text Data + String Functions + Pattern Matching/FTS 🟢 Very Strong أعلى منطقة تداخل واضحة
Date / Time Date/Time Data + PostgreSQL Date & Time 🟢 Very Strong التخصص PostgreSQL يجب أن يبقى extension لا نسخة ثانية
CASE / Conditional Logic Core Query Logic + Interview Bank 🟢 Strong مكرر في interview layer
Subqueries Simple / Correlated / Nested + decision framework 🟢 Very Strong التكرار تعليمي أكثر من كونه فجوة
CTEs CTE Complete Reference + Core Query Logic 🟢 Very Strong Recursive CTE موجود؛ يحتاج مكانًا معماريًا واضحًا
Window Functions Complete Reference Guide 🟢 Very Strong Module مستقل جيد؛ يجب ربطه بالتحليل لا نسخه
JOINs / Cardinality موجودة داخل عدة notes وAdvanced Patterns 🟡 Partial / Scattered يحتاج Module مستقل
Aggregation موجودة ضمن analytics/window/mental models 🟡 Scattered يحتاج Core Aggregation module واضح
Set Operations لا يظهر كـmodule مستقل 🔴 Gap UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT
DDL / DML Temporary Tables وبعض PostgreSQL customization 🟡 Partial INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/ALTER/TRUNCATE غير منظمة كمسار
Transactions / Concurrency لا يظهر كمرجع مستقل 🔴 Gap ACID, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, isolation, locks
Performance / Execution Plans مبادئ عامة داخل Advanced Patterns 🟡 Partial يحتاج EXPLAIN/indexes/sargability/join algorithms
Database Design PK/FK/constraints موجودة 🟡 Partial Normalization, keys, referential actions تحتاج فصلًا
DWH / BI SQL بعض مفاهيم grain/analytics 🟡 Partial يحتاج طبقة مخصصة للـKimball/ETL/ELT SQL
Data Quality / Validation قوي داخل mental models وEDA وAdvanced Patterns 🟢 Strong يمكن تجميعه في module واحد
PostgreSQL Extensions Arrays, FTS, fuzzy matching, custom types/functions 🟢 Strong ممتاز كتخصص منفصل
Interview Prep Interview Master Bank + 99 Questions + Advanced Patterns 🟢 Very Strong تداخل مرتفع بين الصفحات
## 3. Existing Notes — Role in the Future Architecture ### 🧠 Intermediate SQL — Comprehensive Guide Role: المصدر الأساسي للـlearning journey. يغطي حاليًا: schema exploration → numeric/EDA → text → date/time → CASE → subqueries → CTEs → technique selection → case study → window functions. الصفحة نفسها تحتوي mental model قوي وقواعد مثل grain-before-syntax، population-before-metrics، JOIN cardinality، وvalidation. fileciteturn17file0L1-L1 Decision: Keep as the main Learning Path، لكن نقل/ربط كل module في مكان واضح بدل أن تصبح الصفحة نفسها مخزنًا للمحتوى. ### 🧰 SQL — Practical Reference Toolkit Role: Field Manual / Lookup layer. حاليًا تضم Temporary Tables وInterview Master Bank وAdvanced SQL Patterns، وتفصل نفسها صراحةً عن المسار التعليمي. fileciteturn18file0L1-L1 Decision: Keep as a lightweight navigation hub فقط، وليس مكانًا لتكرار الشرح الكامل. ### 🗄️ PostgreSQL Data Manipulation — Master Reference Role: PostgreSQL specialization. يغطي Data Types/Casting، Date & Time، Arrays، String Functions، Pattern Matching/Full-Text Search، Extensions/Fuzzy Matching، Custom Types/Functions، وReal-World Recipes. fileciteturn19file0L1-L1 Decision: Keep as PostgreSQL-only extension layer، مع إزالة/تقليل نسخ المفاهيم العامة الموجودة في Intermediate SQL. ### 📊 SQL Data-Driven Decision Making Role: Analytics application layer. تستخدم SQL لبناء reasoning حول business questions، مع joins وتحليل النتائج. fileciteturn14file2L22-L31 Decision: Keep as applied analytics / case-study layer. ### 📈 SQL Window Functions — Complete Reference Guide Role: Dedicated advanced analytics module. يغطي OVER، ORDER BY/PARTITION BY، ranking، fetching، frames، paging، وغيرها. fileciteturn15file6L65-L75 Decision: Keep standalone، وربطه من Learning Path وAnalytics layer بدل تكرار المحتوى. ### 🎯 Interview Layer 23️⃣ SQL Interview Master Bank يركز على CASE/Subqueries/CTEs، بينما 24️⃣ Advanced SQL Patterns يركز على correctness/performance/maintainability، و99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns يمثل بنك أسئلة أوسع. fileciteturn15file11L119-L127 fileciteturn15file8L85-L96 Decision: Merge conceptually into one Interview Hub with topic-specific banks، بدون حذف المحتوى الحالي. ## 4. Major Overlaps ### 🔴 High overlap - Text/String functions بين Intermediate SQL وPostgreSQL master. - Date/Time بين Intermediate SQL وPostgreSQL master. - CASE/Subqueries/CTEs بين Core Query Logic وInterview Master Bank. - Interview patterns بين 23 / 24 / 99. ### 🟠 Medium overlap - Schema inspection وdata types. - Data quality / NULL handling. - JOIN reasoning موزع في analytics + intermediate + advanced patterns. - Window concepts تظهر جزئيًا في Date/Time ثم بشكل كامل في Window master. ### 🟢 Healthy overlap - نفس المفهوم يظهر في Learning Path ثم Quick Reference ثم Interview/Real-world case؛ طالما أن النسخ ليست كاملة ومكررة. ## 5. Important Gaps to Add Later 1. SQL Foundations — SELECT/FROM/WHERE/DISTINCT/ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET/operators/Boolean logic. 2. JOINs — Complete Reference — INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/CROSS/SELF، semi/anti joins، multi-table joins، cardinality، many-to-many، duplicate multiplication، filtering in ON vs WHERE. 3. Aggregation — Complete Reference — GROUP BY/HAVING، conditional aggregation، COUNT variants، weighted vs unweighted averages، grain changes. 4. Set Operations — UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT. 5. NULL & Three-Valued Logic — IS NULL، COALESCE، NULLIF، NOT IN trap، CASE semantics. 6. DDL / DML — CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE + INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE + UPSERT. 7. Transactions & Concurrency — ACID، BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK، isolation levels، locks، deadlocks. 8. SQL Performance Engineering — EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE، indexes، scans، joins، aggregation, statistics، sargability، CTE materialization. 9. Database Design — normalization/denormalization، natural/surrogate/composite keys، referential actions. 10. SQL for DWH / BI — grain، fact/dimension، snapshots، SCD، surrogate keys، staging/ODS/core/semantic patterns، incremental loads، deduplication. ## 6. Proposed Target Architecture ```txt 🗄️ SQL MASTER LIBRARY │ ├── 00 — Learning Map & Decision Framework ├── 01 — SQL Foundations ├── 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling ├── 03 — Data Types, Casting & NULL Logic ├── 04 — Filtering & Conditional Logic ├── 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning ├── 06 — Aggregation & Grouping ├── 07 — Subqueries & CTEs ├── 08 — Set Operations ├── 09 — Window Functions ├── 10 — Date & Time Analytics ├── 11 — Text, String & Pattern Matching ├── 12 — Analytical SQL Patterns ├── 13 — Data Quality & Validation ├── 14 — SQL Performance Engineering ├── 15 — DDL / DML / Transactions ├── 16 — Database Design ├── 17 — SQL for DWH / BI ├── 18 — PostgreSQL Specialization ├── 19 — Interview Master Hub └── 20 — Practical SQL Toolkit ``` ## 7. Reorganization Rules - Do not delete content because it is duplicated. First identify a canonical home. - Learning Path = sequence and concepts. - Reference = reusable lookup. - PostgreSQL = dialect-specific capabilities. - Analytics = business cases and reasoning. - Interview = questions, traps, trade-offs. - DWH/BI = domain-specific SQL patterns. - A concept should have one canonical deep reference and multiple lightweight links/examples elsewhere. - PostgreSQL-specific syntax should not replace the standard SQL explanation; it should be an extension beneath it. ## 8. Next Step — Actual Restructuring Plan Phase 1 — Inventory: هذه الصفحة. ✅ Phase 2 — Canonical Mapping: لكل note حالية نحدد: Keep / Move / Merge Conceptually / Split / Link Only. Phase 3 — Build Missing Core Modules: Foundations → JOINs → Aggregation → Set Operations → Performance → Transactions → DWH/BI. Phase 4 — Refactor Existing Notes: إزالة التكرار البنيوي مع الحفاظ على المحتوى، وإضافة cross-links بدل النسخ. Phase 5 — Final QA: التأكد أن أي موضوع له مكان واحد واضح، وأن Learning Path لا يحتوي gaps، وأن Interview/Practical/PostgreSQL layers لا تعيد كتابة الـcore content. > الخلاصة: عندك بالفعل قاعدة SQL قوية جدًا. إعادة الهيكلة المطلوبة هي architecture problem أكثر من content problem. أهم خطوة الآن هي تثبيت الـcanonical home لكل topic قبل نقل أي صفحة. ## 9. Phase 2 — Canonical Mapping Matrix > قاعدة المرحلة: لا ننقل أو نحذف أي محتوى الآن. نحدد أولًا الـCanonical Home لكل موضوع، ثم نقرر هل الصفحة الحالية تظل كما هي، تتحول إلى Hub، تُقسم، أو تصبح مجرد رابط/طبقة تطبيقية. ### A. ## 10. Canonical Ownership Rules ### One topic → one deep source - JOINs → one complete canonical reference. - Aggregation → one complete canonical reference. - Window Functions → existing Window Functions master. - Subqueries / CTEs → existing deep references. - Date / Time → general reference + PostgreSQL extension. - Text / String → general reference + PostgreSQL extension. - Performance → future dedicated engineering reference. ### Other pages may contain only one of these: 1. Navigation link to the canonical source. 2. Short contextual explanation needed by that page. 3. Real-world example demonstrating the concept in a different context. 4. Interview question/trap derived from the concept. They should not reproduce the entire canonical explanation. ## 11. Target Architecture — Mapping Existing Content to Final Library ```txt 00 Learning Map │ ├── 01 SQL Foundations [NEW] │ └── SELECT / WHERE / ORDER / DISTINCT / LIMIT / operators │ ├── 02 Database, Schema & Data Modeling [EXISTING + EXPAND] │ └── Exploration / PK / FK / constraints / cardinality / keys │ ├── 03 Data Types, Casting & NULL Logic [MERGE] │ └── Numeric / text / date types / CAST / COALESCE / NULLIF / 3VL │ ├── 04 Filtering & Conditional Logic [EXTRACT] │ └── WHERE / CASE / Boolean logic │ ├── 05 JOINs & Relationship Reasoning [NEW — HIGH PRIORITY] │ └── Join types / cardinality / duplicates / semi / anti / M:N │ ├── 06 Aggregation & Grouping [NEW — HIGH PRIORITY] │ └── GROUP BY / HAVING / conditional aggregation / grain │ ├── 07 Subqueries & CTEs [EXISTING — CONSOLIDATE] │ └── Simple / scalar / correlated / nested / derived / CTE / recursive │ ├── 08 Set Operations [NEW] │ └── UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT │ ├── 09 Window Functions [EXISTING — STRONG] │ ├── 10 Date & Time Analytics [EXISTING — CANONICAL] │ ├── 11 Text, String & Pattern Matching [EXISTING — CONSOLIDATE] │ ├── 12 Analytical SQL Patterns [EXISTING — ANALYTICS] │ ├── 13 Data Quality & Validation [EXTRACT + CONSOLIDATE] │ ├── 14 SQL Performance Engineering [NEW — HIGH PRIORITY] │ ├── 15 DDL / DML / Transactions [NEW — HIGH PRIORITY] │ ├── 16 Database Design [NEW] │ ├── 17 SQL for DWH / BI [NEW — HIGH PRIORITY] │ ├── 18 PostgreSQL Specialization [EXISTING — STRONG] │ ├── 19 Interview Master Hub [MERGE CONCEPTUALLY] │ └── 20 Practical SQL Toolkit [KEEP AS FIELD MANUAL] ``` ## 12. Priority Queue Before Physical Reorganization P0 — Must establish first - JOINs & cardinality - Aggregation & grain - SQL Foundations - NULL / three-valued logic consolidation P1 — High-value engineering gaps - Performance / execution plans / indexes - DDL / DML - Transactions / concurrency - SQL for DWH / BI P2 — Structural completeness - Set Operations - Database Design P3 — Cleanup / presentation - Interview consolidation - PostgreSQL cross-links - Practical Toolkit cross-links - Learning Path navigation cleanup ## 13. Important Decision We are NOT going to physically move the existing pages yet. الـCanonical Mapping أصبح محددًا، لكن النقل الفعلي سيكون بعد إنشاء الـmissing canonical modules، خصوصًا JOINs وAggregation وFoundations. بهذه الطريقة لن نخلق broken links أو ننقل محتوى إلى مكان غير جاهز، وفي نفس الوقت نحافظ على كل المحتوى الحالي. ## 14. Phase 3 — Canonical Modules Created The first P0 canonical modules are now created under Intermediate SQL — Comprehensive Guide: 1. [01 — SQL Foundations — Complete Reference](https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c81f698afea76e9396474) - Foundational mental models - Grain and logical query processing - NULL / three-valued logic - DISTINCT, types, ordering, validation - Core anti-patterns and interview traps 2. [05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning — Complete Reference](https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c81419b2fecc50db92f04) - JOIN semantics and cardinality - Fan-out / row multiplication - JOIN vs EXISTS - LEFT JOIN filtering trap - Bridge tables, self joins, nullable keys - DWH / BI correctness and validation 3. [06 — Aggregation & Grouping — Complete Reference](https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c813a95abc3b25b698b3e) - Aggregation as a grain transformation - COUNT / SUM / AVG and NULL behavior - Conditional aggregation - DISTINCT aggregation - GROUP BY vs window functions - Semi-additive measures - ROLLUP / CUBE / GROUPING SETS - KPI design and validation ### Phase 3 Status Completed: creation of the three missing P0 canonical foundations. Preservation rule: existing SQL notes were not deleted or replaced. These new modules establish canonical ownership so existing pages can later become focused references, case studies, navigation, or interview material without duplicating the deep explanation. ### Next Reorganization Direction The next physical cleanup should consolidate existing content around these owners, with special attention to: - NULL / data-type duplication - aggregation examples scattered across analytics/interview notes - JOIN examples embedded in other pages - duplicate CASE/subquery explanations - PostgreSQL-specific material remaining clearly dialect-specific ## 14. Phase 4 — Physical Reorganization Started The first physical consolidation layer is now in place without deleting legacy content. ### Canonical modules created 1. 01 — SQL Foundations — Complete Reference - Owns SQL mental models, relational basics, grain, logical query processing, NULL/3VL fundamentals, filtering principles, validation mindset, and foundational interview traps. 2. 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning — Complete Reference - Owns JOIN semantics, cardinality, row multiplication, ON vs WHERE, JOIN vs EXISTS/IN, validation, and relationship reasoning. 3. 06 — Aggregation & Grouping — Complete Reference - Owns GROUP BY, aggregate behavior, NULL handling, WHERE vs HAVING, conditional aggregation, pre-aggregation, grain transitions, advanced grouping, and GROUP BY vs window functions. ### Reorganization rule Legacy pages remain intact. They will be progressively converted into navigation, applied examples, dialect-specific extensions, or interview material rather than duplicated canonical references. ### Next consolidation targets - Merge/consolidate Data Types + NULL logic around the canonical ownership model. - Consolidate CASE and Subqueries/CTEs into the 04/07 architecture. - Establish Set Operations as a dedicated canonical module. - Build Performance Engineering, DDL/DML/Transactions, Database Design, and SQL for DWH/BI as the next missing high-value modules. ## 15. Phase 5 — Consolidation Executed The next canonical layer is now established without deleting legacy notes. ### New canonical modules - 03 — Data Types, Casting & NULL Logic — owns type semantics, casting, NULL/3VL, NULL in aggregates and joins, and safe data-quality handling. - 04 — Filtering & Conditional Logic — owns WHERE/predicate reasoning, CASE, filter placement, and conditional classification. - 08 — Set Operations — owns UNION/UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, and set-vs-JOIN decisions. - 14 — SQL Performance Engineering — owns performance reasoning, sargability, execution plans, indexing fundamentals, and optimization anti-patterns. - 15 — DDL, DML & Transactions — owns database changes, write operations, transaction concepts, ACID, isolation, and safe-change patterns. ### Consolidation policy Existing detailed pages remain preserved. Their role is now to provide source material, examples, dialect-specific behavior, or specialized practice. Canonical theory should progressively point to these modules instead of duplicating it. ### Current architecture status 01 Foundations → 02 Database/Schema → 03 Types/NULL → 04 Filtering/CASE → 05 JOINs → 06 Aggregation → 07 Subqueries/CTEs → 08 Set Operations → 09 Window Functions → 10 Date/Time → 11 Text/Pattern → 12 Analytics → 13 Data Quality → 14 Performance → 15 DDL/DML/Transactions → 16 Database Design → 17 DWH/BI → 18 PostgreSQL → 19 Interview → 20 Toolkit Next priority: build 16 Database Design and 17 SQL for DWH / BI, then perform targeted cleanup of legacy pages so they become thin navigation/reference layers rather than competing canonical sources.
